aero.title: Aero break-through: the 105% flush rule and inflated outer-width projection
aero.intro: The ETRTO safety floor and the aero optimum are different questions. Nominal tire width changes with inner width and pressure; this section shows the trend with one formula, while exact installation still follows measured and manufacturer data.

bulbTire.title: ① The bulb-tire aero failure
bulbTire.formula: Inflated tire wider than the rim's maximum outer width
bulbTire.body: The shoulder rolls outward, flow separates early, and the rim loses much of its aero benefit. Crosswind response can also become less stable.

ruleOf105.title: ② The 105% aero flush rule
ruleOf105.formula: Maximum rim outer width ≥ 1.05 × actual inflated tire width
ruleOf105.body: When the rim is flush with or slightly wider than the tire section, flow can reattach to the sidewall and form a more continuous teardrop wing.

modernSweetSpot.title: ③ The modern hookless road sweet spot
modernSweetSpot.formula: 23–25 mm inner width with a 28–32 mm tire
modernSweetSpot.body: Modern wider rims narrow the engineering window where bead support, rolling resistance, and aero transition work together. A broad chart cannot replace a model-specific limit.

aero.current: Current pairing: {rimWidth} mm inner width with a {tireWidth}C tire → about {inflatedWidth} mm inflated → at least {aeroTarget} mm rim outer width to approach the 105% flush target.

traps.title: Frequent failure modes and workshop lessons

nonTleOnHookless.title: Putting an ordinary clincher with a tube on a hookless rim → sudden unseating
nonTleOnHookless.body: Adding a tube does not give an ordinary clincher the bead tensile strength it lacks. A straight hookless wall still has no mechanical hook to resist pressure and side load.
nonTleOnHookless.rule: Rule: a hookless rim requires a tire with TLE / hookless approval.

emptyTpuInflation.title: Inflating a TPU tube in the air → permanent bulges
emptyTpuInflation.body: An unloaded TPU tube can develop irreversible thin spots and bulges when overinflated. Once installed, the uneven wall can fail on the first ride.
emptyTpuInflation.rule: Rule: stay below 0.3 bar (4.3 PSI) before the tube is inside the tire; never test it with an empty CO₂ blast.

oldSealantResidue.title: Leaving dried sealant in an emergency TPU conversion → abrasion wear
oldSealantResidue.body: Dried latex and grit act like sandpaper against a thin TPU wall as the tire rolls and flexes, often producing a leak within a short ride.
oldSealantResidue.rule: Rule: wipe all dried sealant and grit from the casing before inserting the tube.

co2ColdBrittle.title: Using a CO₂ cartridge aggressively → brittle TPU valve
co2ColdBrittle.body: Rapid CO₂ expansion creates a severe temperature drop. The plastic valve base is more vulnerable to brittle fracture under the cold gas pulse.
co2ColdBrittle.rule: Rule: use a hand pump when possible; use CO₂ with a regulator and a slow release.

metalLever.title: Forcing a tight tire with a metal lever → damaged hookless wall
metalLever.body: A straight hookless lip has no hooked curve to spread a point load. A metal lever can crush or delaminate the carbon edge.
metalLever.rule: Rule: never use a metal lever; push both beads into the center well to release circumference.

beadPinch.title: Pinching the bead seat → tire cannot lock into the safety step
beadPinch.body: A trapped tube prevents the tire from seating evenly. It can wobble under pressure and develop a slow leak.
beadPinch.rule: Rule: stop around 1.0 bar, then inspect the rim line all the way around before final inflation.

rimSystem.title: Separate TSS from TC first
rimSystem.body: Hookless TSS and hooked TC rims constrain the bead differently. One system's width window cannot be copied directly to the other.

nominalWidth.title: Nominal width is not measured width
nominalWidth.body: The same nominal width changes with casing, pressure, and rim inner width. This page uses one projection to explain the trend; installation still follows measured and model-specific data.

aeroProjection.title: 105% explains an aero target only
aeroProjection.body: The outer-width target is a display reference for aero shape. It is not a compatibility certification, pressure limit, or bead-retention safety boundary.

items.exactSpecifications: Verify the rim model, tire model, ETRTO, BSD, and the manufacturer's compatibility notes.
items.pressureLimits: Use the strictest limit from the rim, tire, wheelset, and bicycle; this model does not generate a pressure limit.
items.installationCheck: After inflation, check the bead line for even seating, inspect for wobble, and confirm frame and fork clearance.

seo.title: Tire and rim engineering fitment reference
seo.description: Start with this engineering reference model for a narrowed tire-width window, then use the DT Swiss TSS and TC matrix below as broad official comparison material.
seo.articleBody: This page first uses the versioned engineering reference model to calculate a narrowed width window for hookless TSS and hooked TC rims, then shows the DT Swiss broad reference matrix. The two sections use independent methods; DT possible rows and interpolated results remain comparison material and are not model-specific certification.
seo.datasetName: Tire and rim engineering reference model with DT Swiss comparison matrix
seo.datasetDescription: The versioned engineering width windows shown above, followed by backend-provided DT Swiss tire widths, recommended rim internal widths, possible references, and display-only width projections.
seo.measurementTechnique: The page model reads a versioned width window by rim system and inner width; the DT Swiss section separately reads published rows and calculates piecewise references.

methodology.title: DT Swiss comparison note
methodology.unavailable: The backend reference matrix is temporarily unavailable. The page keeps the method and safety limits visible and does not substitute example calculation values.
methodology.body: The DT Swiss table shows broad combinations from the published material. Possible rows and interpolated values are comparison references only; they do not decide the engineering model above and are not certification for a specific rim, tire, or wheelset. Follow the exact model limits during installation.
methodology.version: Model version: {modelVersion}. The limitations below come from the same backend contract.

limitations.modelSpecificCertification: This is a DT Swiss reference chart result, not certification for a specific tire, rim model, or wheelset.
limitations.possibleReferenceStatus: Rows marked possible are reference anchors only; they are never relabeled as recommended.
limitations.interpolationProjection: Interpolated widths are mathematical projections between chart rows and must be checked against the exact manufacturer specifications.
limitations.displayOnlyMetrics: Inflated-width and 105% outer-width values are display-only projections, not measured dimensions or safety limits.

standards.title: Manufacturer Standards
standards.description: The following tables show DT Swiss tire and rim inner-width combinations for hookless (TSS) and hooked (TC) systems as a comparison reference. Their ranges are broad guidance and do not replace fitment information for a specific rim and tire model; follow the applicable manufacturers’ limits when installing.
standards.legendDescription: Recommended combinations are DT Swiss preferred pairings. Possible combinations remain chart references; they must not be relabeled as recommendations or treated as model-specific certification.
